leading_positions.synthesis: Four members (Aili, Aqvist, Brzezinski, Linke) propose the same two-part configuration: base editing credited to David R. Liu alone, and targeted protein degradation credited to Craig M. Crews and Raymond J. Deshaies. They share the three-person arithmetic (Liu plus Crews and Deshaies) and the framing of two designed chemical capabilities with large generative potential. They differ in citation wording: Aili and Brzezinski anchor the degradation part on heterobifunctional PROTACs, Aqvist on the concept and demonstration of induced proximity, Linke on recruitment of the ubiquitin-proteasome system. Several of the four name Komor, Gaudelli, Handa, Ciulli, Gray or Sakamoto as exclusions that the cap forces rather than as a settled judgement of credit, and Aili would fall back on a single-part base-editing trio if the Liu-only credit is judged indefensible.

Six of eight members include B024 in their round-1 configuration, the broadest explicit support for any ballot. Agreement is on the achievement, not the names: five propose Liu alone, while Chabes proposes Liu, Komor and Gaudelli as the whole prize. Chabes, Aqvist and Linke say the Liu-only credit costs Komor and Gaudelli something real, and Chabes and Aqvist leave open the Kondo and Nishida (Target-AID) priority question.

Somfai alone proposes pairing base editing (Liu alone) with palladium-catalysed C-N coupling (Buchwald and Hartwig), a mature, cleanly attributed synthetic method alongside a genome-engineering tool. He holds the pairing loosely and would back B003 alone if the committee prefers a single coherent achievement. Brzezinski and Linke list B003 as an alternative, not as part of their configuration.

Sparr alone proposes ionizable lipid nanoparticles as a single-achievement prize (Cullis, Hope, Madden), on the pKa-tuned charge and non-bilayer phase-behaviour argument and on clinical validation at scale. Aili, Aqvist and Linke list B013 as an alternative. Sparr discloses narrow opening support and proximity to her own field.

Zou alone proposes dye-sensitized solar cells (Gratzel, O'Regan) as a single-achievement prize, on clean attribution and more than thirty years of confirmation, and lists B024 and B060 as alternatives. Zou also names the risk that the technology has been superseded by perovskites.

areas_of_agreement: Base editing (B024) is in six of eight round-1 configurations, and no member disputes that it is a distinct chemical advance with independent replication and clinical entry.
Several members (Aili, Aqvist, Brzezinski, Linke) treat B024 and B009 as a coherent pair, and the three-person cap makes a Liu plus Crews and Deshaies union the only way to carry both.
Members who engage on the point (Aili, Aqvist, Brzezinski, Chabes, Sparr, Zou) accept that Liu is the central originator of base editing, even where they argue Komor and Gaudelli deserve credit.
Opening support is not treated as scientific merit by any member who raises it, and several (Zou, Sparr, Chabes) say so explicitly.
Several members (Aili, Aqvist, Brzezinski, Linke, Sparr, Zou) state that the three-person cap forces exclusions with real claims, and none hides this in their case against.
scientific_disputes: Whether base editing is a new chemical achievement or largely protein engineering and directed evolution on top of the 2020 CRISPR platform: Somfai and Zou press this, Chabes, Sparr and Aqvist say the deaminase-based, double-strand-break-free chemical step is distinct, and Linke says the old deamination chemistry is not the new part but the evolved deaminase and editor architecture are.

Whether degradation by induced proximity is a chemistry achievement or chemical biology: Brzezinski argues that rational heterobifunctional design and ternary-complex energetics are chemistry acting on a biological pathway, answering a chemistry-versus-biology objection that Somfai's exchange with him raised.

Whether ionizable lipid nanoparticles are a physical-chemical concept (Sparr: pKa-tuned charge and bilayer to non-bilayer phase behaviour) or pharmaceutical formulation after the 2023 Medicine prize (raised against B013 by Sparr herself, and by Brzezinski and Chabes).
Whether nitrogenase (B038) can be framed as a definable discovery without a settled catalytic mechanism (Brzezinski, Sparr and Zou doubt it; Brzezinski lists it only as an alternative).
Whether the lasting contribution of the dye-sensitized cell is the architecture or the dyes, and whether perovskites (B060) and dye cells should be treated together or in sequence (Somfai, Zou).
attribution_disputes: B024: Liu alone (Aili, Aqvist, Brzezinski, Linke, Somfai) versus Liu, Komor and Gaudelli (Chabes, and Aili's stated fallback if the Liu-only credit proves indefensible); members disagree whether first-author trainees in a PI-led programme should be laureates and whether the citation text can carry their contribution instead.

B024: whether Kondo and Nishida (Target-AID, a different architecture reported at about the same time) have a priority claim that must change the credited names; Chabes, Aqvist and Zou ask for the priority evidence, and Linke says it should be checked.

B009: whether the credit follows the heterobifunctional PROTAC concept (Crews, Deshaies; Sakamoto and Kim as first authors who cannot be seated) or the cereblon molecular-glue lineage (Handa and Ito), and whether one citation can honour both without merging two histories; Aqvist offered to shift to Handa if the glue lineage is the mature core, and Sparr argues the glue branch is on firmer ground, and Somfai notes that three names would split the two lineages awkwardly.

B013: credit is spread across the Cullis, Hope and Madden group, MacLachlan, and Anderson and Langer, and the priority of the ionizable lipid itself versus the formulation process is contested (Sparr, Brzezinski, Chabes).
B038: structure and mechanism point to different names among Rees, Einsle, Seefeldt, Dean and Ribbe (Brzezinski, Zou).
maturity_disputes: No PROTAC is yet an approved drug (raised by Aili, Aqvist, Brzezinski, Linke, Somfai and Chabes), so Aqvist and Linke would rest the B009 citation on the 2001 concept and its mechanistic validation, not on therapies; Sparr and Somfai would defer it to a later year.

Base editing is about ten years from the originating papers; Chabes, Aili and Aqvist count independent replication and clinical entry as sufficient, while Chabes notes that durability, bystander and off-target editing are still being measured.

Palladium-catalysed C-N coupling has no maturity doubt, but Somfai, Brzezinski and Linke note that the 2010 cross-coupling prize and the Kosugi and Migita precursors make it look incremental to some members.
Dye-sensitized solar cells carry no maturity question but face the argument that a prize would honour a superseded technology (Zou, Somfai).
Biomolecular phase separation (B047) was ranked low or listed as an alternative by Brzezinski, Linke and Sparr because the in vivo evidence for liquid-like assemblies is still debated.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Sparr states that her first choice (B013) sits close to her own field and that she ranks it first partly for that reason; she does not state a formal conflict or recusal.
No member discloses a personal, institutional or collaborative conflict with any credited name, and no recusal is requested in any of the eight round-1 files.
questions_for_round2: If B024 is paired with B009, is a Liu-alone credit defensible, or does the committee judge that excluding Komor and Gaudelli makes the citation untenable, in which case B024 must stand as a single-achievement prize? Members who propose a Liu-alone credit should say what the citation text would say about the decisive first-author papers.

What is the documented priority record for Kondo and Nishida (Target-AID) relative to Komor et al. 2016 and Gaudelli et al. 2017, and does it change who can be credited for base editing or only how the citation is worded?

For B009, does the committee credit the heterobifunctional PROTAC concept (Crews, Deshaies), the cereblon molecular-glue lineage (Handa), or neither this year? If PROTACs, can the citation rest on the 2001 concept and mechanism despite the absence of an approved PROTAC drug?

Is a prize that pairs base editing and degradation a coherent chemical-biology prize, or does it share a theme only loosely, and does Somfai's B003 pairing or a single-achievement prize (B024, B003, B013 or B025) offer a more defensible citation? Each proposer should say which step in their achievement is the discovery.

Does base editing read as a distinct chemical achievement or a follow-on to the 2020 CRISPR prize? Members on both sides should specify which part, the evolved deaminase, the editor architecture or the double-strand-break-free outcome, they would put in the citation.

For B013, which specific step (the pKa-tuned ionizable lipid or the formulation process) would the citation recognise, can it be cut to three names, and does the 2023 Medicine prize leave it distinct enough for a Chemistry citation?

Should B003, B038, B025 and B060 be kept in the final-ballot pool given that each has a single proposer or alternative-only support in round 1, and what additional evidence would members need on the 2010 overlap (B003), the unresolved mechanism (B038), or the dye versus perovskite lineage (B025, B060)?
summary.chair_observation: Round 1 concentrated on base editing: six of eight configurations include B024, and four of those pair it with degradation (B009) and the same three names. The other four configurations propose different pairings or single-achievement prizes (B024 alone, B024 with B003, B013, B025), so apparent convergence on B024 is not yet convergence on a citation or a set of laureates. The chair's own configuration is one of the four B024 plus B009 proposals, and this summary counts only positions stated in the eight round-1 files. The main open questions are the Liu-only versus trio credit for B024, the Target-AID priority record, and whether the PROTAC or the cereblon glue lineage carries B009.
